question: What can an encounter with Fakir Mohan’s Randi Pua Ananta and the actor’s preparation add to the literature-to-cinema story?

sources.author: MCL bureau

sources.inspection: Full displayed article opened; Ananta section, lines 63–80, read directly. Scope of primary evidence is the quoted speakers’ own accounts.

findings: The complete displayed original story was read by Anvesha; Drishti independently checked the village-work paragraphs. Fruit-taking troubles the villagers, while digging and thatching bring them to Ananta for help. This is a reading of fiction, not a social survey or an assertion about the film’s scenes.
The director’s interview identifies the literary source. Mishra’s own words explain the audience encounter he hoped for; they do not establish reception or commercial success.
coverage_decision: Enhance one existing Literature and Screen section. A dedicated Ananta page is not needed to carry this compact encounter; existing Bhukha and Pratikshya connections remain.
public_change: Replace the listing-only sentence with two short paragraphs and two numeric notes; no new image, title controversy, plot ending or generic reflection.
retained_for_future: Mohapatra says consultation with writers preceded the decision to use Ananta as the film title while retaining the source story’s title in its attribution. Retain for future adaptation research; not necessary to expand this article into a title controversy.
limitations: No original first-publication date, imprint or critical-edition claim.
No assumption that these episodes appear in Ananta2025.
No inference about real writer compensation from a fictional character’s response to payment.
No medical or intellectual-disability diagnosis inferred from narration.
No audio audition, actor interpretation or complete-film viewing.
Promotional claims about industry revival or the story’s historical role in a language movement were not independently established and are not adopted.
Body-weight and diet details are unnecessary to the literary encounter and are not reproduced.
Location, drinking-water intervention and safety claims remain unverified testimony and are not adopted.
No festival award, collection total, source-author compensation or complete-film comparison is inferred.

The interview is first-person testimony within a published report. Trailer-title and inaccessible poster discoveries are not treated as viewing or credit verification.
next_action: Investigate Pushkara as a possible distinct contemporary literature-to-screen case: locate its original source work and a primary film-source credit before proposing new prose. Reuse performer-contributions evidence and the Ananta interview only as discovery leads. Do not repeat completed Ananta or Malajanha searches, or reopen exhausted payment, booklet and exact Sadhana-title gaps without an identifiable new source.
